exam.tagline: AIPB's four-part national bookkeeping credential — the experience-based benchmark for full-charge bookkeepers.
exam.description: The Certified Bookkeeper (CB) is the national bookkeeping credential from the American Institute of Professional Bookkeepers (AIPB), established as the benchmark for full-charge bookkeepers. It is earned through a four-part exam: two closed-book tests at Prometric — Adjustments & Error Correction and Payroll & Depreciation — plus two open-book workbook finals on Inventory and Internal Controls & Fraud Prevention. Candidates also need about two years of bookkeeping experience (or 3,000 part-time hours) within three years of passing and must agree to the AIPB Code of Ethics. With a 75% pass mark on the Prometric parts and 70% on the workbook finals, the CB signals professional competence in the adjustments and controls that separate a bookkeeper from a data-entry clerk.

quickAnswer.summary: The AIPB Certified Bookkeeper (CB) is a four-part national credential: two closed-book Prometric tests (Adjustments & Error Correction; Payroll & Depreciation) and two open-book workbook finals (Inventory; Internal Controls & Fraud Prevention). You also need ~2 years of bookkeeping experience and must sign the AIPB Code of Ethics.
advantages: Nationally recognized benchmark for full-charge bookkeepers
Experience-based, not degree-based — open to working bookkeepers
Covers the adjustments, controls, payroll, and fraud prevention employers value
Backed by the AIPB Code of Ethics and a 300+ location Prometric network

roadmap: Confirm you have (or will earn) ~2 years of bookkeeping experience
File the paper application and pay the registration fee
Wait for AIPB to issue your testing ID number
Schedule and pass Prometric Parts 1 & 2 (2 hours each)
Complete the open-book Inventory and Internal Controls workbook finals
Submit experience proof and sign the Code of Ethics to receive the CB
exam.prerequisites: There is no education prerequisite. You must, however, meet the experience requirement (about 2 years full-time or 3,000 part-time/freelance hours) and sign the AIPB Code of Ethics to be awarded the designation.
exam.eligibility: The CB is open to working bookkeepers without a degree. You may take the exam before finishing the experience requirement, but you must accumulate at least two years of full-time bookkeeping experience (or 3,000 hours of part-time/freelance work) within three years of passing the exam. Undergraduates may count internships and accounting-related volunteer work such as VITA. You apply by mailing a signed paper application to AIPB, which then issues a testing ID number.

examMeta.questions: Multiple-choice; item counts per test are not published. Six tests total: two 2-hour Prometric tests per part for Parts 1–2, plus untimed workbook finals for Parts 3–4
examMeta.time: 2 hours each for Prometric Parts 1 & 2; Parts 3–4 are untimed open-book finals
examMeta.pass: 75% on Prometric Parts 1 & 2; 70% on workbook Parts 3 & 4
examMeta.fee: Registration $25 member / $60 nonmember (nonrefundable) + $100 each for Prometric Parts 1 & 2; Parts 3–4 have no exam fee (study workbooks extra)
examMeta.format: Closed-book computerized tests at Prometric (Parts 1–2); open-book workbook finals (Parts 3–4)
examMeta.admin: American Institute of Professional Bookkeepers (AIPB); Prometric delivers Parts 1–2

topics.name: Part 1, Test 1 — Adjustments
topics.note: Accruals, deferrals, and the adjusted trial balance; month-end financial statement preparation

topics.name: Part 1, Test 2 — Error Correction & Bank Reconciliation
topics.note: Locating bookkeeping errors, trial-balance analysis, and reconciling bank accounts

topics.name: Part 2, Test 1 — Payroll
topics.note: Worker classification, withholding, deposits, Forms W-4/941/940/W-2/W-3, and payroll journal entries

topics.name: Part 2, Test 2 — Depreciation
topics.note: Book vs tax depreciation, straight-line and accelerated GAAP methods, units-of-production, MACRS basics

topics.name: Part 3 — Inventory
topics.note: Perpetual vs periodic systems, FIFO/LIFO/weighted-average, shrinkage, lower of cost or net realizable value (open-book workbook final)

topics.name: Part 4 — Internal Controls & Fraud Prevention
topics.note: Segregation of duties, noncash asset theft, check/credit-card fraud, vendor scams, and computer fraud controls (open-book workbook final)

examEssentials: 2 yrs full-time or 3,000 hrs part-time within 3 yrs
Required to be awarded the designation
timeline: Within 1 year of application (parts in any order)

costBreakdown.footnote: Registration is nonrefundable. Retakes: $60 per Prometric test after a 30-day wait; Parts 3–4 may be retaken at no cost.

exam.time: Study + testing typically several months; experience within 3 years of passing

faqs.q: How is the AIPB CB exam structured?
faqs.a: It is a four-part exam. Parts 1 and 2 are closed-book, multiple-choice tests taken at a Prometric center — Adjustments & Error Correction, and Payroll & Depreciation — each with a 2-hour limit. Parts 3 and 4 are untimed, open-book finals at the back of the Mastering Inventory and Mastering Internal Controls and Fraud Prevention workbooks.

faqs.q: What score do I need to pass?
faqs.a: You need 75% on each Prometric part (Parts 1 and 2) and 70% on each workbook final (Parts 3 and 4). You can take the parts in any order and keep credit for any part you pass.

A nonrefundable registration fee of $25 for AIPB members or $60 for nonmembers, plus $100 each for the two Prometric parts — a $225–$260 minimum before study workbooks or prep. The two workbook finals carry no separate exam fee.

You need at least two years of full-time bookkeeping experience or 3,000 hours of part-time/freelance work, which can be completed within three years of passing the exam. Internships and accounting-related volunteer work may count for students.

faqs.q: How do I keep the CB active?
faqs.a: Certified Bookkeepers must complete 60 continuing professional education (CPE) hours every three years, beginning on the anniversary of the last certification test passed. AIPB-approved providers supply the CPE.

summaryPoints: Four-part exam: two 2-hour Prometric tests (75% to pass) plus two untimed open-book workbook finals (70%).
Requires ~2 years of bookkeeping experience and signing the AIPB Code of Ethics to be awarded.
Minimum direct cost is $225 (member) / $260 (nonmember) before study workbooks.
Renew with 60 CPE hours every 3 years through AIPB-approved education.

program.about: The American Institute of Professional Bookkeepers (AIPB) is the bookkeeping profession's national association and awards the Certified Bookkeeper (CB) designation, the recognized benchmark for full-charge bookkeepers. The CB requires passing a four-part exam and demonstrating about two years of experience, then agreeing to the AIPB Code of Ethics. AIPB maintains a network of approved continuing-education providers for credential upkeep.

registrationSteps.title: Confirm experience track
registrationSteps.description: Plan to show at least 2 years of full-time bookkeeping experience (or 3,000 part-time/freelance hours) within three years of passing the exam. Students may count internships and accounting-related volunteer work.

registrationSteps.title: File the paper application
registrationSteps.description: Complete and mail the signed CB application with the nonrefundable registration fee ($25 AIPB member / $60 nonmember). Allow about 4 weeks for AIPB to process it.

registrationSteps.title: Receive your testing ID
registrationSteps.description: Once approved, AIPB mails a testing identification number you use to schedule Prometric appointments.

registrationSteps.title: Schedule and pass Prometric Parts 1 & 2
registrationSteps.description: Book the two closed-book computer tests at a Prometric center in any order: Adjustments & Error Correction, and Payroll & Depreciation (2 hours, 75% to pass each). You get your score immediately.

registrationSteps.title: Complete the workbook finals (Parts 3 & 4)
registrationSteps.description: Finish the open-book Inventory and Internal Controls & Fraud Prevention finals included in the study workbooks (untimed, 70% to pass). Submit them to AIPB for grading.

registrationSteps.title: Submit experience and ethics, get the CB
registrationSteps.description: Provide the experience evidence form(s) and sign the AIPB Code of Ethics. AIPB issues your certificate within about two weeks of the last requirement.

program.proctoring: Parts 1 and 2 are closed-book, computerized tests delivered at Prometric Test Centers (300+ U.S. locations) with live center proctoring. Parts 3 and 4 are open-book workbook finals completed at home and submitted to AIPB.
program.retakePolicy: If you fail a Prometric part, you may retake just that test after a 30-day waiting period for a $60 fee (you keep credit for any part you passed). The open-book workbook finals (Parts 3–4) may be retaken at no cost.
program.recertification: Certified Bookkeepers must complete 60 continuing professional education (CPE) hours every three years, measured from the anniversary of the last certification test passed. CPE must come from AIPB-recognized providers; failure to meet the requirement can result in revocation of the designation.
program.scoreReporting: Prometric prints your score at the center immediately after Parts 1 and 2. Workbook finals (Parts 3–4) are graded by AIPB after submission; results are reported to you and reflected in your AIPB record.
program.refundPolicy: The registration fee is nonrefundable. Prometric test fees are generally nonrefundable once scheduled, though you can cancel or reschedule without penalty if you contact Prometric at least two days before the appointment.
program.providersNote: Prometric delivers the closed-book parts; AIPB grades the workbook finals directly. Study workbooks (Mastering Inventory; Mastering Internal Controls and Fraud Prevention) can be bought individually or as a bundle, and the CB is distinct from the NACPB CPB license.

orgFaqs.q: Do I need a degree to earn the CB?
orgFaqs.a: No. The CB is experience-based, not degree-based. You need about two years of bookkeeping experience (or 3,000 part-time hours), which can be earned within three years of passing the exam.

orgFaqs.q: Can I take the Prometric parts in any order?
orgFaqs.a: Yes. Although labeled Part 1 and Part 2, the two Prometric tests may be taken in any order, and credit is kept for any part you pass even if you later retake another.

orgFaqs.q: How do I maintain the designation?
orgFaqs.a: Complete 60 AIPB-approved CPE hours every three years and stay in good standing with the AIPB Code of Ethics. Approved providers include AIPB's own courses and recognized partners.
